name: GSE221988, Singlet Research Alpha
description: Generation of Locus Coeruleus Norepinephrine Neurons from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells [snRNA-seq] (GSE221988), reprocessed from raw reads in Singlet Research Alpha (October 2026): 2 samples that passed QC, 9,859 called cells, Homo sapiens, reference GRCh38-2024-A. Gene counts (spliced and unspliced), splice junctions, cell calls and per-cell QC in one .s1 object per sample, with per-cell Cell Ontology cell type, chromosomal sex and genetic ancestry labels. Data CC0 1.0; code MIT.
citeAs: Generation of Locus Coeruleus Norepinephrine Neurons from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells [snRNA-seq]. GEO accession GSE221988, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE221988. Reprocessed in Singlet Research Alpha (October 2026), https://singlet.bio/study/GSE221988.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Alignment and counting (singlet pipeline 0.3.0, reference GRCh38-2024-A)

rai:dataCollection: Raw sequencing reads of GEO series GSE221988 (submitted ?), downloaded from SRA, and GEO's sample metadata. No new samples were collected.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: GEO series GSE221988 and its SRA runs (prov:wasDerivedFrom lists the run used per sample).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: One pipeline (singlet) for every sample: raw reads from SRA (the first sequencing run of each sample, at most its first 30 million reads); barcode and UMI layout detected from the reads; alignment and counting with STARsolo against one reference per species (human GRCh38, GENCODE v44; mouse GRCm39, vM33; rat mRatBN7.2; macaque Mmul_10; zebrafish GRCz11).

Exonic (spliced) and intronic (unspliced) molecules are counted separately for every cell, with splice junctions. In Alpha a molecule touching both an exon and an intron, a molecule in nested genes, or a multi-mapping read split across workers can be counted twice (2% to 19% per cell).

Cells were called with the STARsolo CellRanger2.2 knee filter; every barcode with at least 100 reads is stored, so cells can be called again. The cells table also carries an EmptyDrops call (called_ed) that is not the default.

Sample QC (functions/_shared/qc-rules.ts): a sample is described here only when its count matrix is not empty, at least one cell was called, at least 20% of reads mapped and the median cell has at least 30 genes. Samples below that are flagged low QC (kept in the study's files, left out of these documents and of every count); samples with under 5% of reads mapped and a median under 10 genes are removed.
Files were transcoded to the .s1 format (one immutable object per sample, pz2-coded matrices) and verified member by member against the files they replace.

Research Alpha release policy alpha-2026-10-27e: samples whose reads do not match the expected strand, libraries that are not gene expression (antibody, hashtag, guide, V(D)J or chromatin), samples with no called cell, and studies aligned to a genome other than the species GEO records are left out; a study left with no sample is withheld.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Per-cell labels are computed by the pipeline, with no human annotator: Cell Ontology cell type by a hierarchical, marker-guided labeller (levels: 1 compartment, 2 lineage, 3 cell type, 4 and deeper subtype; levels 1 and 2 are the default, 3 and deeper are previews); chromosomal sex from XIST against chrY expression (human and mouse); continental genetic ancestry (HANCESTRO) by supervised admixture against 1000 Genomes reference panels, for human donors with enough covered sites.

Sample metadata are GEO's text, mapped to UBERON (tissue), MONDO (disease; healthy is PATO:0000461), HsapDv / MmusDv (developmental stage), PATO (sex), HANCESTRO (self-reported ancestry) and Cell Ontology (sorted cell type), by rules or by a model; each *_mapping column of the samples record set says which.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Automated, in the pipeline: singlet-annotate 0.2.0; no human annotators.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Per cell: one cell-type path (with a confidence per level), one chromosomal sex call, at most one ancestry call. Per sample: one value per ontology field, several where GEO lists several.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cell type, per-study accuracy against CELLxGENE author labels: compartment 0.84, lineage 0.75, cell type 0.43, subtype 0.32. The score ranks calls; it is not a calibrated probability.
Chromosomal sex: 153 of 156 called samples (98.1%) agree with the sex in GEO; the 3 disagreements were GEO errors. About 13% of human cells stay ambiguous.
Genetic ancestry: validated on donors simulated from 1000 Genomes and on 22 donors with self-reported ancestry.
rai:dataBiases: All 2 samples GEO lists for GSE221988 are in this document.
Organism: Homo sapiens; assay: 10x-arc-gex. A study is one lab's design: its tissues, donors and conditions are what the depositors chose.
Genetic ancestry is called for 2 of 2 samples here; across the atlas it covers about 1% of cells.
Only studies whose raw reads are in SRA and could be processed are included; GEO metadata is uncurated.
rai:dataLimitations: Labeller accuracy recorded in this study's files (manifest annotations.cell_type.per_study_accuracy): level 1 (compartment) 0.842, level 2 (lineage) 0.747, level 3 (cell type) 0.428, level 4 (subtype) 0.32; levels from 3 are previews.

Alpha used only the first sequencing run of each sample and at most 30 million reads (the median sample used 10% of its deposited reads). Against the authors' own Cell Ranger results on 135 samples, Alpha finds a median of 65% of their cells, with a quarter of their UMIs per cell.
Some molecules are counted twice (2% to 19% per cell); counts depend slightly on the thread count; the spliced and unspliced layers are not suited to RNA velocity.
Cell type labels: per-study accuracy compartment 0.84, lineage 0.75, cell type 0.43, subtype 0.32; levels 3 and deeper are previews.
Chromosomal sex agrees with GEO for 98.1% of samples; about 13% of human cells stay ambiguous, mostly in pools of both sexes or samples with few reads per cell.
Genetic ancestry is computed only for human donors with enough genotype coverage (under 1,000 samples, about 1% of cells); elsewhere it is missing. Mixed ancestry is reported as admixed.

Transcriptomics only: antibody tags (ADT), hashtags (HTO), ATAC, spatial coordinates, CRISPR guides and V(D)J clonotypes are not served. Doublet, ambient-RNA and mitochondrial allele layers are not in Alpha.

GEO metadata (sex, tissue, disease) is not curated and may be wrong. A cell or sample count in the catalog can differ from the QC inside a file; the file is the truth. A sample GEO lists under two series is in both studies, so atlas-wide totals count it twice.
Known issues and what Beta changes: https://singlet.bio/known-issues
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: All studies are public GEO deposits whose raw reads are public in SRA; no new human data was collected.

Genotypes, mitochondrial allele data and the raw genotype inputs of the labeller are never stored in the released files or served. Per cell, only chromosomal sex (female / male / ambiguous) and continental genetic ancestry (HANCESTRO group) are released.
GEO sample characteristics (which may include age, sex, ancestry, disease and donor ids chosen by the depositors) are kept as GEO publishes them.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating models of single-cell gene expression (cell-type classifiers, representation and foundation models) on uniformly processed counts.
Cross-study meta-analysis and cohort building by organism, tissue, disease, cell type, sex or ancestry.
Benchmarking analysis methods on many studies processed the same way; re-calling cells from the stored barcodes.
Not validated for clinical use or for identifying individuals.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Uniform reprocessing makes public single-cell studies comparable and reusable without running a pipeline per study. Models trained on it inherit its skew toward human and mouse, toward the tissues and assays most often deposited, and toward the donors with ancestry calls; the dataBiases field gives the numbers.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Per-sample .s1 objects and label sidecars are immutable and content-addressed (the key contains the digest); a change writes a new object, and the study manifest (mutable) gets a new rev. Which samples and studies are served is set by the Research Alpha release policy; this document's version is the policy id in force (alpha-2026-10-27e). Research Alpha (October 2026) is a feedback-oriented research preview. Beta, a full re-run with a new engine, is estimated for Q1 2027 and will be released separately. Feedback from any page of https://singlet.bio; known issues at https://singlet.bio/known-issues.

Cell type levels: 1 compartment, 2 lineage, 3 cell type, 4 subtype; the level of a call is the number of ids in cell_type_path.

recordSet.name: cell_qc
recordSet.description: One record per stored barcode (called or not): the 'cells' member (CEL2 columnar table, docs/format-s1.md section 5.3) of each .s1 object, at the byte range the manifest gives. Row i is column i of the sample's matrices. Read it with the singlet Python or R package (singlet.load); mlcroissant cannot decode the .s1 container. Other columns in this study's cells tables: cc_listed, cc_pvalue, cyc_phase, cyc_s_score, cyc_g2m_score, qc_n_reads, don_donor_id, don_prob_max, don_best_singlet, don_best_doublet, don_cell_status.

field.description: The default cell call (STARsolo knee filter). Matrix columns with called = false are uncalled barcodes.

field.name: called_ed

recordSet.name: spliced_counts
recordSet.description: Spliced (exonic) counts, cells x features, as non-zero (col, row, count) entries: member 'exon_counts.1pz' of each .s1 object, a pz2 matrix (docs/format-s1.md section 4) stored column- (cell-) chunked with a chunk index, so any range of cells is one HTTP range request. Rows are merged exons of the reference genes (pack a34ebca652f38b28f0ab5c0ec2a13249, 310,797 rows); the features record set gives each gene's rows, and summing a gene's rows gives gene-level counts. Read with the singlet package (modalities "spliced"; "counts" is spliced + unspliced).
